title: readSurface
body:
## readSurface

Reads one VTK XML polydata file (.vtp): polygonal surfaces, lines and vertices with point and cell arrays, such as extracted boundaries, slices or streamlines saved earlier. Use it to reopen surface artifacts, for instance in a later workflow that renders or measures them. Use readParallelPolyData for partitioned .pvtp output and readUnstructuredGrid for volume meshes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Only one file is read; reopen a time series through its .pvd collection with pvPVDReader, or use pvXMLPolyDataReader with several files.

Native constructor: `XMLPolyDataReader`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Each file is expected to be in the VTK XML polygonal dataset format. The standard extension is .vtp. If more than one file is specified, the reader will switch to file series mode in which it will pretend that it can support time and provide one file per time step. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"minItems":1,"maxItems":1}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "readSurface",
  "options": {
    "files": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
